ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Partial reversal

A patient receiving enoxaparin develops serious bleeding, and a clinician administers protamine as part of treatment. Laboratory testing still detects some anti-Xa activity afterward. Which explanation best fits this finding?

  1. Protamine only partially neutralizes LMWH anti-Xa activity
  2. Protamine intensifies all enoxaparin effects
  3. Protamine is an irreversible factor Xa inhibitor
  4. Protamine restores vitamin K synthesis within minutes
  5. Protamine converts enoxaparin to thrombin
Answer and explanation

Protamine only partially neutralizes LMWH anti-Xa activity

Unlike UFH reversal, LMWH neutralization by protamine is incomplete.

Option explanations

Protamine only partially neutralizes LMWH anti-Xa activity: Unlike UFH reversal, LMWH neutralization by protamine is incomplete.

Protamine intensifies all enoxaparin effects: Protamine is used to reduce heparin activity, not uniformly intensify it.

Protamine is an irreversible factor Xa inhibitor: Protamine is not a direct Xa inhibitor.

Protamine restores vitamin K synthesis within minutes: Vitamin K synthesis is unrelated to protamine reversal.

Protamine converts enoxaparin to thrombin: No conversion of enoxaparin into thrombin occurs.
